excerpt: OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that AGI (artificial general intelligence) benefits all of humanity. To pursue that mission, we are committed to safely developing and deploying highly capable AI systems, which create significant benefits and also bring new risks.
paraphrase: OpenAI states its mission to ensure AGI benefits humanity and its commitment to safely developing capable AI systems that bring both benefits and risks.

excerpt: We build for safety at every step and share our learnings so that society can make well-informed choices to manage new risks from frontier AI.
paraphrase: OpenAI commits to building safety throughout development and sharing findings to help society manage frontier AI risks.

excerpt: The Preparedness Framework is OpenAI’s approach to tracking and preparing for frontier capabilities that create new risks of severe harm.
paraphrase: The document defines the Preparedness Framework as OpenAI's approach to tracking and preparing for frontier capabilities that create severe harm risks.

excerpt: We currently focus this work on three areas of frontier capability, which we call Tracked Categories:
paraphrase: OpenAI states it currently focuses on three Tracked Categories of frontier capability.

context_stem: We currently focus this work on three areas of frontier capability, which we call Tracked Categories:
excerpt: Biological and Chemical capabilities that, in addition to unlocking discoveries and cures, can also reduce barriers to creating and using biological or chemical weapons.
paraphrase: Biological and chemical capabilities offer scientific benefits but can also lower barriers to creating weapons.

context_stem: We currently focus this work on three areas of frontier capability, which we call Tracked Categories:
excerpt: Cybersecurity capabilities that, in addition to helping protect vulnerable systems, can also create new risks of scaled cyberattacks and vulnerability exploitation.
paraphrase: Cybersecurity capabilities can protect systems but also enable larger-scale cyberattacks and exploitation.

context_stem: We currently focus this work on three areas of frontier capability, which we call Tracked Categories:
excerpt: AI Self-improvement capabilities that, in addition to unlocking helpful capabilities faster, could also create new challenges for human control of AI systems.
paraphrase: AI self-improvement capabilities can accelerate beneficial progress but may also challenge human control over AI systems.

excerpt: In each area, we develop and maintain a threat model that identifies the risks of severe harm and sets thresholds we can measure to tell us when the models get capable enough to meaningfully pose these risks.
paraphrase: For each area, OpenAI maintains a threat model identifying severe harm risks and measurable capability thresholds.

excerpt: We won’t deploy these very capable models until we’ve built safeguards to sufficiently minimize the associated risks of severe harm.
paraphrase: OpenAI commits to withholding deployment of highly capable models until sufficient safeguards exist.

excerpt: This Framework lays out the kinds of safeguards we expect to need, and how we’ll confirm internally and show externally that the safeguards are sufficient.
paraphrase: The document describes expected safeguards and how their sufficiency will be confirmed internally and demonstrated externally.

excerpt: In this updated version of the Framework we also introduce a set of Research Categories.
paraphrase: This version introduces new Research Categories.

excerpt: These are areas of capability that could pose risks of severe harm, that do not yet meet our criteria to be Tracked Categories, and where we are investing now to further develop our threat models and capability elicitation techniques.
paraphrase: Research Categories are capabilities with potential severe harm risk that don't yet meet Tracked Category criteria but warrant investment in threat modeling and elicitation.

excerpt: We are constantly refining our practices and advancing the science, to unlock the benefits of these technologies while addressing their risks.
paraphrase: OpenAI states an ongoing commitment to refining practices and science to balance benefits and risks.

excerpt: This revision of the Preparedness Framework focuses on the safeguards we expect will be needed for future models more capable than those we have today.
paraphrase: This revision focuses on anticipated safeguards for future, more capable models.

excerpt: By “severe harm” in this document, we mean the death or grave injury of thousands of people or hundreds of billions of dollars of economic damage.
paraphrase: The footnote defines severe harm as thousands of deaths/grave injuries or hundreds of billions of dollars in economic damage.
stated_bar: thousands of people or hundreds of billions of dollars of economic damage

excerpt: Our safety stack addresses a broad spectrum of risks, including many with harms below this severity.
paraphrase: OpenAI notes its broader safety stack covers risks below the severe harm threshold too.

excerpt: In choosing to set a high bar here, we aim to ensure that the most severe risks receive attention commensurate with their magnitude.
paraphrase: OpenAI explains it set a high severity bar so the most severe risks get proportionate attention.

excerpt: We believe there are a limited number of AI capabilities that could pose new risks of severe harm.
paraphrase: OpenAI believes only a limited set of AI capabilities pose new severe harm risks.

excerpt: In order to safely unlock the beneficial uses of frontier AI capabilities, we exercise particular caution and implement safeguards that sufficiently minimize the risk of severe harm in these areas.
paraphrase: OpenAI exercises caution and implements safeguards to minimize severe harm risk while unlocking beneficial uses.

excerpt: To do this, we:
paraphrase: Lead-in to the list of activities OpenAI undertakes.

excerpt: Decide where to focus – we use a holistic risk assessment to decide which frontier capability categories to track or research further, and to define threshold levels of those capabilities that are associated with meaningful increases in risk of severe harm.
paraphrase: OpenAI uses holistic risk assessment to select which capability categories to track and to set thresholds tied to meaningful risk increases.

excerpt: Measure capabilities associated with risks of severe harms – we run in–scope models through frontier capability evaluations to measure the full extent of model capabilities before we deploy our models and during development.
paraphrase: OpenAI runs in-scope models through capability evaluations both before deployment and during development.

context_stem: Measure capabilities associated with risks of severe harms —
excerpt: Our capability elicitation efforts are designed to detect the threshold levels of capability that we have identified as enabling meaningful increases in risk of severe harms.
paraphrase: Capability elicitation efforts aim to detect when identified risk-relevant capability thresholds are reached.

excerpt: Safeguard against severe harms – we evaluate the likelihood that severe harms could actually occur in the context of deployment, using threat models that take our safeguards into account.
paraphrase: OpenAI evaluates likelihood of severe harm occurring in deployment context using threat models incorporating safeguards.

excerpt: We do not deploy models that reach a High capability threshold until the associated risks that they pose are sufficiently minimized.
paraphrase: Models reaching High capability thresholds are not deployed until their risks are sufficiently minimized.

excerpt: If a model under development reaches a Critical capability threshold, we also require safeguards to sufficiently minimize the associated risks during development, irrespective of deployment plans.
paraphrase: Models reaching Critical capability thresholds during development require safeguards regardless of deployment plans.

excerpt: Build trust – we engage with subject–matter experts across and beyond OpenAI to inform these efforts and to build confidence that we are meeting our commitments and effectively managing risk.
paraphrase: OpenAI engages internal and external experts to build confidence it is meeting commitments and managing risk effectively.

excerpt: An internal, cross-functional group of OpenAI leaders called the Safety Advisory Group (SAG) oversees the Preparedness Framework and makes expert recommendations on the level and type of safeguards required for deploying frontier capabilities safely and securely.
paraphrase: The Safety Advisory Group, a cross-functional internal leadership group, oversees the Framework and recommends safeguard levels and types.

excerpt: OpenAI Leadership can approve or reject these recommendations, and our Board’s Safety and Security Committee provides oversight of these decisions.
paraphrase: OpenAI Leadership approves or rejects SAG recommendations, with Board oversight via the Safety and Security Committee.

section_heading: 1.1 Why we're updating the Preparedness Framework

paraphrase: Introduces four ways the environment is changing.

section_heading: 1.1 Why we're updating the Preparedness Framework
context_stem: Our environment is changing in four key ways:
excerpt: Safeguarding stronger models will require more planning and coordination. Until now, our models’ own limitations have given us confidence that, in the areas tracked under the Preparedness Framework, they were safe to deploy.
paraphrase: Stronger models will need more planning and coordination; previously, model limitations gave confidence models were safe to deploy in tracked areas.

section_heading: 1.1 Why we're updating the Preparedness Framework
context_stem: Safeguarding stronger models will require more planning and coordination —
excerpt: Our evaluations have so far shown that even our most advanced models, even without safeguards in place, aren’t yet capable enough to pose severe risks in areas like bio- or cybersecurity.
paraphrase: Evaluations so far show even the most advanced models, unsafeguarded, aren't capable enough to pose severe risks in bio or cybersecurity.

section_heading: 1.1 Why we're updating the Preparedness Framework
context_stem: Safeguarding stronger models will require more planning and coordination —
excerpt: We are on the cusp of systems that can do new science, and that are increasingly agentic - systems that will soon have the capability to create meaningful risk of severe harm.
paraphrase: OpenAI is approaching systems capable of new science and increased agency, soon posing meaningful severe harm risk.

section_heading: 1.1 Why we're updating the Preparedness Framework
context_stem: Safeguarding stronger models will require more planning and coordination —
excerpt: This means we will need to design and deploy safeguards we can rely on for safety and security – which requires a new level of planning and coordination across the company, beyond what’s needed to measure capabilities.
paraphrase: OpenAI will need reliable safety and security safeguards requiring new company-wide planning and coordination beyond capability measurement.

section_heading: 1.1 Why we're updating the Preparedness Framework
context_stem: Our environment is changing in four key ways:
excerpt: More frequent deployments require scalable evaluations. Today, we’re able to develop and deploy better models more often than ever thanks to reasoning advances that can unlock new capabilities without as much training as the previous paradigm.
paraphrase: More frequent deployments due to reasoning advances require scalable evaluation methods.

section_heading: 1.1 Why we're updating the Preparedness Framework
context_stem: More frequent deployments require scalable evaluations —
excerpt: As a result, it’s important to embrace methods that scale, including scalable capability evaluations that work well for a faster cadence of model deployment, as well as periodic deeper dives that validate those scalable evaluations.
paraphrase: OpenAI emphasizes scalable capability evaluations plus periodic deeper validation reviews to match faster deployment cadence.

section_heading: 1.1 Why we're updating the Preparedness Framework
context_stem: Our environment is changing in four key ways:
excerpt: A highly dynamic development landscape for frontier AI makes it important for us to share our latest thinking. With a growing number of labs producing frontier AI models, it is more important than ever for us and other labs to contribute to community efforts on frontier safety and security,
paraphrase: A dynamic frontier AI landscape with growing numbers of labs makes it important to share thinking and contribute to community safety efforts.

section_heading: 1.1 Why we're updating the Preparedness Framework
context_stem: A highly dynamic development landscape for frontier AI makes it important for us to share our latest thinking —
excerpt: including by adapting safety work for the reasoning paradigm and for increasingly agentic systems, and advocating for and contributing to advanced protection measures in a world of continual frontier AI proliferation.
paraphrase: This includes adapting safety work for reasoning models and agentic systems, and advocating for advanced protections amid continual AI proliferation.

section_heading: 1.1 Why we're updating the Preparedness Framework
context_stem: Our environment is changing in four key ways:
excerpt: We and the broader field have gained more experience and built conviction on how to do this work. The past year of research and deployment on safety frameworks both at OpenAI and across the AI field have given us greater clarity on how to prioritize and approach categories of risk.
paraphrase: A year of research and deployment experience at OpenAI and across the field has clarified how to prioritize and approach risk categories.

section_heading: 1.1 Why we're updating the Preparedness Framework
context_stem: We and the broader field have gained more experience and built conviction on how to do this work —
excerpt: This includes our threat modelling, development work on new capability evaluations, and external consultations, as well as relevant publications from external researchers and updated frameworks from industry peers.
paraphrase: This experience includes threat modeling, capability evaluation development, external consultations, and peer publications and frameworks.

section_heading: 1.1 Why we're updating the Preparedness Framework
excerpt: For example, our adoption of Capability Reports and Safeguards Reports parallels Anthropic’s updated RSP.
paraphrase: The footnote notes OpenAI's Capability and Safeguards Reports parallel Anthropic's updated RSP.

excerpt: We evaluate whether frontier capabilities create a risk of severe harm through a holistic risk assessment process.
paraphrase: A holistic risk assessment process is used to evaluate whether frontier capabilities create severe harm risk.

excerpt: This process draws on our own internal research and signals, and where appropriate incorporates feedback from academic researchers, independent domain experts, industry bodies such as the Frontier Model Forum, and the U.S. government and its partners, as well as relevant legal and policy mandates.
paraphrase: The risk assessment draws on internal research and, where appropriate, external feedback from academics, experts, industry bodies, and government, plus legal/policy mandates.

excerpt: Where we determine that a capability presents a real risk of severe harm, we may decide to monitor it as a Tracked Category or a Research Category.
paraphrase: Capabilities determined to present real severe harm risk may be monitored as Tracked or Research Categories.

excerpt: Tracked Categories are those capabilities which we track most closely, measuring them during each covered deployment and preparing safeguards for when a threshold level is crossed.
paraphrase: Tracked Categories are closely monitored capabilities, measured at each covered deployment, with safeguards prepared for threshold crossings.

excerpt: We treat a frontier capability as a Tracked Category if the capability creates a risk that meets five criteria:
paraphrase: A capability qualifies as a Tracked Category if its risk meets five specified criteria.

context_stem: We treat a frontier capability as a Tracked Category if the capability creates a risk that meets five criteria:
excerpt: Plausible: It must be possible to identify a causal pathway for a severe harm in the capability area, enabled by frontier AI.
paraphrase: Criterion 1: a plausible causal pathway to severe harm enabled by frontier AI must be identifiable.

context_stem: We treat a frontier capability as a Tracked Category if the capability creates a risk that meets five criteria:
excerpt: Measurable: We can construct or adopt capability evaluations that measure capabilities that closely track the potential for the severe harm.
paraphrase: Criterion 2: capability evaluations must be constructible or adoptable that closely track severe harm potential.

context_stem: We treat a frontier capability as a Tracked Category if the capability creates a risk that meets five criteria:
excerpt: Severe: There is a plausible threat model within the capability area that would create severe harm.
paraphrase: Criterion 3: a plausible threat model within the area must be capable of creating severe harm.

context_stem: We treat a frontier capability as a Tracked Category if the capability creates a risk that meets five criteria:
excerpt: Net new: The outcome cannot currently be realized as described (including at that scale, by that threat actor, or for that cost) with existing tools and resources (e.g., available as of 2021) but without access to frontier AI.
paraphrase: Criterion 4: the outcome must be currently unachievable without frontier AI using existing tools/resources such as those available in 2021.

context_stem: We treat a frontier capability as a Tracked Category if the capability creates a risk that meets five criteria:
excerpt: Instantaneous or irremediable: The outcome is such that once realized, its severe harms are immediately felt, or are inevitable due to a lack of feasible measures to remediate.
paraphrase: Criterion 5: harm realized must be either immediately felt or inevitable due to lack of feasible remediation.

excerpt: We review and update Tracked Categories periodically or when we learn significant new information.
paraphrase: Tracked Categories are reviewed and updated periodically or upon significant new information.

excerpt: Research Categories are capabilities that, while they do not meet the above criteria, nonetheless have the potential to cause or contribute to severe harm, and where we are working now in order to prepare to address risks in the future (including potentially by maturing them to Tracked Categories).
paraphrase: Research Categories are capabilities not meeting Tracked Category criteria but with potential to contribute to severe harm, prompting current preparatory work.

excerpt: For each Tracked Category, we develop and maintain a threat model identifying specific risks of severe harms that could arise from the frontier capabilities in that domain and sets corresponding capability thresholds that would lead to a meaningful increase in risk of severe harm.
paraphrase: For each Tracked Category, a threat model identifies severe harm risks and sets capability thresholds indicating meaningful risk increases.

excerpt: SAG reviews and approves these threat models.
paraphrase: SAG reviews and approves the threat models.

excerpt: Capability thresholds concretely describe things an AI system might be able to help someone do or might be able to do on its own that could meaningfully increase risk of severe harm.
paraphrase: Capability thresholds concretely describe assisted or autonomous actions that could meaningfully increase severe harm risk.

excerpt: High capability thresholds mean capabilities that significantly increase existing risk vectors for severe harm.
paraphrase: High capability thresholds are defined as capabilities significantly increasing existing severe harm risk vectors.

excerpt: Covered systems that cross this capability threshold are required to have robust and effective safeguards that sufficiently minimize the associated risk of severe harm before they are deployed and appropriate security controls as they are developed.
paraphrase: Systems crossing the High threshold require robust safeguards minimizing risk before deployment and appropriate security controls during development.

excerpt: Critical capability thresholds mean capabilities that present a meaningful risk of a qualitatively new threat vector for severe harm with no ready precedent.
paraphrase: Critical capability thresholds are capabilities presenting a meaningfully new, unprecedented severe harm threat vector.

excerpt: Critical capabilities require safeguards even during the development of the covered system, irrespective of deployment plans.
paraphrase: Critical capabilities require safeguards during development regardless of deployment plans.

excerpt: These criteria were informed in part by Meta’s recent Frontier AI Framework.
paraphrase: Footnote acknowledges Meta's Frontier AI Framework informed these criteria.

excerpt: Threat models are informed both by our broader risk assessment process, and by more specific information that we gather across OpenAI teams and external experts.
paraphrase: Threat models draw on both the broader risk assessment process and specific information gathered internally and externally.

excerpt: While past deployment experiences are an important source of information about existing risks, we also recognize that in the case of net-new risks of severe harm, significant safeguards may be needed to reduce the risk of harms that have never been realized.
paraphrase: Past deployment experience informs risk understanding, but net-new severe harm risks may require significant safeguards even absent realized harms.

excerpt: Our team develops or adopts evaluations designed to track progress on each of these capabilities and to indicate when the identified capability thresholds may have been reached.
paraphrase: The team develops or adopts evaluations to track capability progress and flag when thresholds may be reached.

paraphrase: Table 1 further details capability thresholds, associated risks, and safeguards.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: AI Self-improvement (now a Tracked Category), Long-range Autonomy and Autonomous Replication and Adaptation (now Research Categories) are distinct aspects of what we formerly termed Model Autonomy.
paraphrase: The former Model Autonomy category has been split: AI Self-improvement is now a Tracked Category, while Long-range Autonomy and ARA are now Research Categories.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: We have separated self-improvement because it presents a distinct plausible, net new, and potentially irremediable risk, namely that of a hard-to-track rapid acceleration in AI capabilities which could have hard-to-predict severely harmful consequences.
paraphrase: Self-improvement was separated out because of its distinct plausible, net-new, potentially irremediable risk of rapid, hard-to-track capability acceleration with unpredictable severe consequences.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: In addition, the evaluations we use to measure this capability are distinct from those applicable to Long-range Autonomy and Autonomous Replication and Adaptation.
paraphrase: Self-improvement uses distinct evaluations from those used for Long-range Autonomy and ARA.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: Meanwhile, while these latter risks’ threat models are not yet sufficiently mature to receive the scrutiny of Tracked Categories, we believe they justify additional research investment and could qualify in the future, so we are investing in them now as Research Categories.
paraphrase: Long-range Autonomy and ARA threat models aren't mature enough for Tracked Category status but merit investment now as Research Categories, with potential future qualification.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: Nuclear and Radiological capabilities are now a Research Category.
paraphrase: Nuclear and Radiological capabilities have been reclassified as a Research Category.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: While basic information related to nuclear weapons design is available in public sources, the information and expertise needed to actually create a working nuclear weapon is significant, and classified.
paraphrase: Basic nuclear design information is public, but actually building a working weapon requires significant, classified expertise.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: Further, there are significant physical barriers to success, like access to fissile material, specialized equipment, and ballistics.
paraphrase: Significant physical barriers, such as access to fissile material and specialized equipment, also stand in the way.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: Because of the significant resources required and the legal controls around information and equipment, nuclear weapons development cannot be fully studied outside a classified context.
paraphrase: Resource requirements and legal controls mean nuclear weapons development cannot be fully studied outside classified contexts.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: Our work on nuclear risks also informs our efforts on the related but distinct risks posed by radiological weapons.
paraphrase: Nuclear risk work also informs efforts on the related but distinct radiological weapon risks.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: We build safeguards to prevent our models from assisting with high-risk queries related to building weapons, and evaluate performance on those refusal policies as part of our safety process.
paraphrase: Safeguards prevent model assistance with high-risk weapons queries, with refusal policy performance evaluated as part of the safety process.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: Our analysis suggests that nuclear risks are likely to be of substantially greater severity and therefore we will prioritize research on nuclear-related risks.
paraphrase: Analysis suggests nuclear risks are substantially more severe, so nuclear-related research will be prioritized.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: We will also engage with US national security stakeholders on how best to assess these risks.
paraphrase: OpenAI will engage US national security stakeholders on assessing these risks.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: Persuasion: OpenAI prohibits the use of our products to manipulate political views as part of our Model Spec, and we build in safeguards to back this policy.
paraphrase: OpenAI's Model Spec prohibits using products to manipulate political views, backed by safeguards.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: We also continue to study the persuasive and relational capabilities of models (including on emotional well-being and preventing bias in our products) and monitor and investigate misuse of our products (including for influence operations).
paraphrase: OpenAI studies persuasive/relational model capabilities, including emotional well-being and bias, and monitors/investigates misuse such as influence operations.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: We believe many of the challenges around AI persuasion risks require solutions at a systemic or societal level, and we actively contribute to these efforts through our participation as a steering committee member of C2PA and working with lawmaker and industry peers to support state legislation on AI content provenance in Florida and California.
paraphrase: OpenAI believes persuasion risk challenges need systemic solutions and contributes via C2PA steering committee membership and support for state content provenance legislation in Florida and California.

section_heading: Changes to Tracked Categories in version 2
excerpt: Within our wider safety stack, our Preparedness Framework is specifically focused on frontier AI risks meeting a specific definition of severe harms, and Persuasion category risks do not fit the criteria for inclusion.
paraphrase: The Preparedness Framework specifically targets severe-harm-defined frontier risks, and Persuasion risks do not meet that inclusion criteria.
